brief.meaningEn: Something given deliberate attention when planning, instead of being considered only afterwards.
brief.meaningZh: 某事在規劃時已獲刻意重視，而不是事後才考慮。
brief.grammar: make X a priority rather than an afterthought; treat X as a priority rather than an afterthought; a priority can be one of several important considerations. Afterthought contrasts late consideration, not necessarily an event happening late.
brief.register: Natural contrast between planning importance and belated consideration, not an opaque idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 列為重點，不表示其他事情一概取消；要指出規劃時如何預留時間或資源。
brief.misconceptionZh: 事後補做仍可能有用，但與一開始已納入規劃不同；不能只憑事情發生的先後，判斷重視程度。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說清要提早納入哪項需要，提出規劃中的實際安排。

listening.promptZh: 哪項安排顯示已提早考慮？

options.en: An evening and responsibilities for reading drafts were agreed before the printing date was fixed.
options.zh: 定下印刷日期前，已議定互讀初稿的晚上及分工。

options.en: Draft reading was added only after the copies had already been printed.
options.zh: 所有成品印好後，才加上互讀初稿的安排。

options.en: Each person would submit a final version without a shared discussion.
options.zh: 每人會各交最終版本，不作共同討論。

options.en: The evening was reserved for distributing finished copies rather than discussing drafts.
options.zh: 那晚預留作派發成品，而不是討論初稿。

listening.explanationZh: 互讀時間及分工已提早納入規劃，不是印好後才加上、各自交最終版本，或只安排派發成品。
listening.en: We made time to read each other’s drafts a priority rather than an afterthought: before fixing the printing date, we reserved an evening for questions and agreed who would bring each version.
listening.zh: 我們把互讀初稿的時間列為規劃重點，不留待事後才想起：定下印刷日期前，已預留一晚討論問題，並議定由誰帶哪個版本。

reply.promptEn: Why did you reserve that evening before choosing the printing date?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼先預留那一晚，才選印刷日期？

options.en: We wanted questions about the drafts to have time in the plan.
options.zh: 我們想在計劃中預留時間，處理初稿的疑問。

options.en: Reading together needed a real slot before printing, not spare time afterwards.
options.zh: 互讀需要在印刷前有實際時段，而不是事後才找空閒時間。

options.en: We wanted draft reading to be a priority rather than an afterthought.
options.zh: 我們想把互讀初稿列為重點，不是事後才考慮。

options.en: Agreeing the evening first protected a chance to discuss changes while they were still possible.
options.zh: 先議定那晚，可在仍能修改時保留討論機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了提早把討論納入規劃的目的，並不是說必須先消除所有疑問。

scene.promptZh: 故事小組先排好每分鐘的演出，最後才想到字幕，發現沒有時間核對文字。現在他們正補做核對，但你要描述的是原來的規劃。哪句最準確？

options.en: Captions were an afterthought in the original plan, even though the group is checking them now.
options.zh: 字幕是原計劃中事後才想起的部分，雖然小組現在正補做核對。

options.en: Checking captions now shows that time for them was reserved at the start.
options.zh: 現在核對字幕，表示一開始已為它們預留時段。

options.en: The original plan treated captions as its first priority before setting the performance times.
options.zh: 原計劃先把字幕列為首要重點，才定下演出時間。

scene.explanationZh: 事後補做核對，不等於一開始已有安排；需要分清原來規劃與現在的補救。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨顯示「X was a priority rather than an afterthought」？

options.en: The team only remembered X after committing all its time to other tasks.
options.zh: 小組把時間全分給其他工作後，才想起 X。

options.en: The plan reserved a named time for X before setting the final deadline.
options.zh: 定下最後期限前，計劃已為 X 預留明確時間。

options.en: The group asked about the resources X needed while planning the work.
options.zh: 規劃工作時，小組已問 X 需要哪些資源。

contrast.explanationZh: 把時間分給其他工作後才想起 X，最不能支持它已提早列為重點的說法；早期安排需要有具體根據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「下次也先定印刷日期，互讀有空才加吧？」你想保留修改機會。哪句最好？

options.en: Let us make draft reading a priority rather than an afterthought, and agree its evening before the printing date.
options.zh: 先把互讀初稿列為重點，不留待事後才想起；定下印刷日期前，先議定互讀的晚上吧。

options.en: We can use the collection evening for draft questions, even though the copies will already be printed.
options.zh: 雖然到時已印好，仍可在取書那晚處理初稿疑問。

options.en: Let us choose the date by the number of finished covers and leave reading time outside the schedule.
options.zh: 按已完成的封面數量選日期，把互讀時間留在時間表以外吧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需要在仍可修改時留討論機會，不只在取成品時提問題，也不能以封面進度代替互讀安排。

speaking.en: I want this to be a priority rather than an afterthought, so let us give it a place in the plan before fixing the deadline.
speaking.zh: 我想把這件事列為重點，不留待事後才想起，所以定下期限前，先在計劃中為它預留位置。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明提早納入的需要及具體安排。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想每周三陪祖母整理她的家庭食譜，卻總在答應額外義工工作後才看有沒有空。祖母說不想每次等最後通知。你想在接受下一項工作前，先問她是否願意預留周三一小時，同時承認她也可以選別的時間。用一至兩句英文直接向祖母提出安排。

examples.en: I want our recipe hour to be a priority rather than an afterthought, so I will check with you before accepting extra work on Wednesdays. Would that hour still suit you, or would you prefer another time?
examples.zh: 我想把我們整理食譜的時間列為重點，而不是事後才考慮，所以接受周三的額外工作前，我會先跟你確認。那一小時仍適合你嗎，還是你比較想選另一個時間？

examples.en: Time with you should be a priority rather than an afterthought in my week. Could we agree a recipe hour before I take on another optional task, without assuming Wednesday must suit you?
examples.zh: 陪伴你的時間應在我每周的安排中列為重點，而不是事後才想起。接受另一項可選的工作前，我們可否先議定整理食譜的時間，而不假定周三一定適合你？

glossary.zh: 我們整理食譜的一小時

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出在接額外工作前先商量陪伴時間的安排，並讓祖母選擇；不把重視對方變成替她決定，也不假稱時段已獲同意。

takeaways.en: Access questions were a priority rather than an afterthought when the group chose the venue and wrote the invitation.
takeaways.zh: 小組選場地及寫邀請時，已把通達需要列為重點，不是事後才考慮。

takeaways.en: He wanted family time to be a priority rather than an afterthought, so he discussed the weekend before accepting another shift.
takeaways.zh: 他想把家庭時間列為重點，不留待事後才考慮，所以答應另一班工作前，先商量周末的安排。

brief.meaningEn: Watch or monitor someone or something, often for a developing change or a possible need.
brief.meaningZh: 留意或持續照看某人、某事，常為察覺變化或需要。
brief.grammar: keep/kept/keeping an eye on + object; monitor rather than necessarily stare continuously or control the outcome. Distinguish keeping one’s eye on the ball, meaning focus on what matters.
brief.register: Common informal idiom, suitable for a request to watch something for a while.
brief.boundaryZh: 留意不表示能阻止變化，或已解決問題；要說清誰留意甚麼，以及何時通知誰。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不需要真的閉上一隻眼，也不表示負責留意的人可以決定所有相關安排。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出清楚的留意請求，準確報告所見及觀察時段。

listening.promptZh: 請求的工作及權限是甚麼？

options.en: Watch for a start-time change and tell the group, without independently rearranging slots.
options.zh: 留意開始時間有沒有改變，並通知小組，而不自行重排時段。

options.en: Rewrite the timetable while the speaker collects the props.
options.zh: 說話者取道具時，重寫時間表。

options.en: Take the props to the organiser instead of looking at the timetable.
options.zh: 不看時間表，改把道具帶給統籌。

options.en: Check only that the group’s name is spelt correctly, without watching for time changes.
options.zh: 只核對小組名稱的拼寫，不留意時間變動。

listening.explanationZh: 請求是留意時段變化並通知小組，不是授權重排，也不只是核對名稱。
listening.en: Please keep an eye on the rehearsal timetable while I collect the props; if the start moves, tell our group, but ask the organiser before changing anyone’s slot yourself.
listening.zh: 我去取道具時，請留意排練時間表；如果開始時間改了，請告訴我們小組，但自行調動別人的時段前，要先問統籌。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want someone to watch the timetable?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼想有人留意時間表？

options.en: I will be collecting props and could miss a change to our start time.
options.zh: 我會去取道具，可能錯過開始時間改動。

options.en: They can keep an eye on it while I am away from the rehearsal area.
options.zh: 我離開排練區時，他們可以繼續留意。

options.en: A message about a changed start would let our group know when to be ready.
options.zh: 通知開始時間的改動，可以讓小組知道何時需要準備好。

options.en: The timetable may change while I am doing another task.
options.zh: 我處理另一項工作時，時間表可能有所改動。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回答了分工及避免錯過變化的目的，不把留意當成可以自行重排。

scene.promptZh: 朋友請你煮茶時看着水壺，水滾便叫他；他沒有請你換茶葉或改他的煮茶方法。哪句準確？

options.en: He asked me to keep an eye on the kettle and tell him when the water boiled.
options.zh: 他請我留意水壺，水滾時告訴他。

options.en: He asked me to choose a different tea recipe before watching the kettle.
options.zh: 他請我先選另一種煮茶方法，才看水壺。

options.en: He wanted me to leave the kettle and return only after he had poured the tea.
options.zh: 他想我離開水壺，等他倒茶後才回來。

scene.explanationZh: 留意的對象及需要通知的時點已明確，並沒有改煮茶方法或離開的請求。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從 keep an eye on the timetable 推論出來？

options.en: Someone is asked to monitor it.
options.zh: 有人被請求留意時間表。

options.en: The observer now has permission to change other groups’ times.
options.zh: 負責留意的人現在獲准改動別組的時間。

options.en: The context may specify which changes to report.
options.zh: 情境可以說明需要報告哪些變化。

contrast.explanationZh: 留意與獲授權改動是兩回事，需要另有安排。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你請我看時間表，我看到延遲就直接把別組調走吧？」統籌仍掌管時段。哪句最好？

options.en: Please keep an eye on the changes and tell us; the organiser still needs to agree any rearrangement.
options.zh: 請留意改動並告訴我們；重排仍需要統籌同意。

options.en: Move the next group first and tell the organiser after they arrive.
options.zh: 先調走下一組，等他們到場才告訴統籌。

options.en: Watch the old printed sheet instead of the updated timetable, so we keep the original plan.
options.zh: 只看舊的印刷時間表，不看更新版本，這樣便保留原計劃。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留留意及通知的分工，不擅自改動其他組的安排，也不用舊表代替現行資料。

speaking.en: I can keep an eye on the changes and tell you what I notice, but I will check before altering the arrangement.
speaking.zh: 我可以留意改動，並告訴你觀察所得，但更改安排前會先詢問。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清觀察、通知及改動的權限。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你昨天替書展留意入口隊伍，記得十時至十一時隊伍變短，之後便交更離開。伙伴想報告寫「全日沒有擠塞」，但你未看之後情況。用一至兩句英文提供自己的觀察及時段，請接更者補資料。

examples.en: I kept an eye on the entrance queue from ten to eleven and saw it become shorter. Please ask the next volunteer about the later hours before describing the whole day.
examples.zh: 我在十時至十一時留意入口隊伍，看見隊伍變短；描述全日情況前，請先問接更義工之後幾小時的情況。

examples.en: While I was keeping an eye on the entrance, the queue eased, but I left at eleven. My notes cover that hour; the next volunteer can tell us what happened afterwards.
examples.zh: 我留意入口時，隊伍有所紓緩，但我十一時已離開；我的筆記只涵蓋那一小時，之後情況可以問接更義工。

glossary.zh: 我的筆記涵蓋那一小時

writing.selfCheckZh: 提供已觀察的變化及時間限制，請接更者補充；不把一小時的觀察擴為全日結論。

takeaways.en: She kept an eye on the parcel shelf while her friend looked for the missing label.
takeaways.zh: 朋友找遺失標籤時，她留意放包裹的架子。

takeaways.en: We are keeping an eye on the replies so we can tell the host which questions still need an answer.
takeaways.zh: 我們持續留意回覆，好告訴主持哪些問題仍待回答。

sources.sentence: My grandfather taught me to mind the pennies.

brief.meaningEn: Pay careful attention to small expenses.
brief.meaningZh: 仔細留意小額開支。
brief.grammar: mind the pennies; mind/minded/minding; pennies stand for small sums, not necessarily literal penny coins. Related to the proverb about pounds, but this phrase alone gives no guarantee about all finances.
brief.register: Conventional informal money wording. Use a concrete fictional spending example without judging a person’s worth from spending or income.
brief.boundaryZh: 留意小額開支，不表示只買最便宜的東西或忽略品質，也沒有說整體預算一定足夠。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要看每項小開支及累積影響，不能只因單項便宜，就認為整體合用。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪些小額支出需要記錄，同時考慮實際需要，以及仍待核對的總額。

listening.promptZh: 小組為甚麼記下每包小裝飾的花費？

options.en: Repeated small purchases had reduced the money reserved for a necessary material.
options.zh: 重複的小額購買，減少了留給必要物料的錢。

options.en: The model was finished without needing any glue or other supplies.
options.zh: 模型已完成，不再需要膠水或其他用品。

options.en: They were counting the number of houses rather than recording purchases.
options.zh: 他們只是在數房屋，而不是記錄購買。

options.en: One decoration pack had cost more than all the other materials combined.
options.zh: 一包裝飾花費，比其餘所有物料加起來還多。

listening.explanationZh: 重點是小額花費累積，佔用了膠水的預留款；不是單包極貴、在數房屋，或已不需要物料。
listening.en: For our model village, we started minding the pennies by noting each small pack of decorations; the price of one pack looked minor, but repeated purchases used money we had meant to keep for glue.
listening.zh: 製作模型村時，我們開始留心小額開支，把每包小裝飾的花費記下；單包看來花費不多，重複購買卻用了本來想留作買膠水的錢。

reply.promptEn: Why did you begin recording the little decoration purchases?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼開始記下那些小額裝飾購買？

options.en: The small amounts were adding up and using our glue money.
options.zh: 小額花費加起來，用了本來留作買膠水的錢。

options.en: Minding the pennies would help us see where the repeated spending went.
options.zh: 留心小額開支，可讓我們看見重複花費去了哪裏。

options.en: Looking at one pack at a time had hidden the effect of buying several.
options.zh: 只逐包看，會掩蓋連續買幾包的影響。

options.en: We needed to compare the combined decoration cost with what we still required.
options.zh: 我們需要比較裝飾的總開支，以及仍然需要的物料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以小額累積及必要物料解釋記錄的目的，不把留意花費當成要取消所有裝飾。

scene.promptZh: 虛構社團要印一份清楚可讀的資料卡。兩種紙張每張的價錢差別很小，但薄紙需要印兩次才看得清。若要衡量實際的小額開支，哪句最合適？

options.en: We should mind the pennies by comparing the usable copies’ total cost, not just the price of one sheet.
options.zh: 應留心小額開支，比較可用成品的總成本，不只看單張紙價。

options.en: The lower price per sheet settles the choice before we consider the second printing.
options.zh: 考慮第二次印刷之前，單張較便宜已足以決定選哪款。

options.en: A small difference means there is no need to record either paper purchase.
options.zh: 差額小，表示兩款紙都不需記錄開支。

scene.explanationZh: 應把重印納入實際可用成品的成本；小額不等於可以忽略，也不只是選表面單價最低的一款。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由 someone minds the pennies 得出？

options.en: They pay attention to small expenses.
options.zh: 他們留意小額開支。

options.en: They have already proved their whole budget will cover every need.
options.zh: 他們已證明，整體預算足以涵蓋每項需要。

options.en: They may record small purchases that add up over time.
options.zh: 他們可以記下日積月累的小額購買。

contrast.explanationZh: 留心一類開支，不表示已核對全部需要及總預算。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「要留心小錢，下次乾脆不要買膠水，裝飾先照買吧？」模型零件仍要黏合。哪句最好？

options.en: Minding the pennies means noticing the repeated costs, not dropping the glue we still need; let us total the decorations first.
options.zh: 留心小額開支，是要看重複花費，不是刪掉仍需要的膠水；先加總裝飾開支吧。

options.en: Choose the smallest decoration packs each time, without adding the repeated purchases together.
options.zh: 每次選最小的裝飾包，不用把重複購買的花費加起來。

options.en: We can treat the glue money as spare because each decoration pack costs little.
options.zh: 每包裝飾都便宜，所以可以把膠水的預留款當成餘款。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先看累積花費及必要材料。單包小或便宜，都不能代替合計，也不表示預留款可以隨意使用。

speaking.en: We are minding the pennies by recording small purchases and checking what the project still needs.
speaking.zh: 我們記下小額購買，也查看項目還需要甚麼，藉此留心小額開支。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把小額累積與實際需要連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說中的家庭對話。孩子以為爸爸記下每次買材料的小額花費，是嫌她的手作沒價值；爸爸想說自己願支持，記錄是為看清還可留多少買必需品，而非責怪她。用一至兩句英文寫爸爸直接回答。

examples.en: I am minding the pennies so we can see what is left for the materials you still need, not because I think your project is unimportant. Let us look at the small purchases together and choose what will be useful next.
examples.zh: 我留心小額開支，是想看還剩多少錢買你仍需要的材料，不是覺得你的手作不重要。我們一起看看那些小額購買，再選下一樣有用的東西吧。

examples.en: Your project matters to me, and minding the pennies helps us talk honestly about the money available. I would like us to review the little purchases together, rather than have you think I am blaming you.
examples.zh: 我重視你的項目，留心小額開支讓我們可以坦誠談可用的錢。我想一起檢視那些小額購買，而不是讓你以為我在責怪你。

glossary.en: look at the small purchases together

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出實際親子回應，分清留意花費與否定興趣；邀請孩子一起看記錄，不把收入、需要或手作價值變成對人的評價。

takeaways.en: The volunteers minded the pennies by checking the small delivery charges before ordering the exhibition cards.
takeaways.zh: 義工訂展覽卡前，先核對小額運費，藉此留心小額開支。

takeaways.en: She was minding the pennies, but she still chose paper that visitors could read without a second printing.
takeaways.zh: 她留心小額開支，但仍選擇訪客不用重印也看得清楚的紙張。

lessons.titleZh: 朝有希望或合適的方向前進

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The improved results show that we are on the right track.

brief.meaningEn: Following a course that seems suitable or likely to lead towards the intended aim.
brief.meaningZh: 正循看來合適或有望達到所定目標的方向前進。
brief.grammar: be/seem/on the right track with something; evidence may support a direction without establishing final success. The intended goal matters when judging right.
brief.register: Common journey metaphor for promising progress or a suitable line of thought.
brief.boundaryZh: 有進展的跡象，不代表已完成或必定成功；也需要說清楚是相對於哪個目標。
brief.misconceptionZh: 別人喜歡成果的某一面，不一定顯示自己的主要目標已達到；方向仍可以重新評估。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體根據判斷方向，分清有希望、仍待測試及已完成的情況。

listening.promptZh: 這次證據支持甚麼範圍？

options.en: The first-room trial is promising, while other routes and versions still need checking.
options.zh: 第一個房間的試用結果有希望，但其他路線及版本仍需要核對。

options.en: The small trial established how readers used every floor and print version.
options.zh: 小規模試用已確立，讀者怎樣使用每一層樓及每種印刷版本。

options.en: Newcomers could find the room only after the team gave them spoken directions.
options.zh: 新人只在小組口頭指路後，才找到房間。

options.en: The guide’s progress was judged solely by how many copies were printed.
options.zh: 指南進展只按印了多少份判斷。

listening.explanationZh: 新來者找到第一個房間的結果，支持目前方向，但樓上及大字版仍未測試；判斷也不只是看印刷數量。
listening.en: The revised visitor guide seems on the right track: in our small trial, newcomers found the first room without asking, but we have not yet checked the upper-floor route or the larger print version.
listening.zh: 新版訪客指南看來方向對了：在小規模試用中，新來者不用問路便找到第一個房間，但我們還未核對樓上路線及大字版。

reply.promptEn: Why do you think the revised guide is promising?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼覺得新版指南有希望？

options.en: Newcomers used it to find the first room without asking.
options.zh: 新人能用它自行找到首個房間。

options.en: That small trial gives us a concrete sign that the change helps with our aim.
options.zh: 小規模試用給了具體跡象，顯示改動有助於我們的目標。

options.en: We seem on the right track because the first route worked for the people who tried it.
options.zh: 試用的人能走通首條路線，所以方向看來對了。

options.en: The result supports continuing with the revision and checking the remaining routes.
options.zh: 結果支持我們繼續修訂，並核對餘下路線。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用實際試用結果解釋有希望的方向，不把有限結果當作所有工作已完成。

scene.promptZh: 學生想寫一個讓讀者清楚分辨兩位敘述者的故事，朋友卻只讚封面漂亮，還沒讀正文。你想判斷學生在這個目標上的進展。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The cover praise alone does not show whether the narration is on the right track.
options.zh: 單憑對封面的稱讚，未能看出敘事是否朝合適方向前進。

options.en: The friend has already read a sample and correctly identified each narrator.
options.zh: 朋友已讀過試讀片段，並正確辨認每位敘述者。

options.en: The next test should ask only whether readers can remember the characters’ names, rather than who is narrating.
options.zh: 下一次試讀只應問讀者記不記得人物名字，而不是由誰敘述。

scene.explanationZh: 目標是讓讀者分清敘述者，卻還沒有正文試讀的資料。記得人物名字也不等於知道由誰敘述，應用相關讀者的實際理解作判斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「We seem on the right track」推出？

options.en: There is some reason to think the direction is suitable.
options.zh: 有些根據讓人覺得方向合適。

options.en: The intended result has already been achieved in full.
options.zh: 想要的成果已全部達到。

options.en: The group can explain the signs supporting its judgement.
options.zh: 小組可解釋支持判斷的跡象。

contrast.explanationZh: seem 及方向合適，都不等於所有成果已完成；可以交代判斷根據，以及仍需核對的範圍。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「新來者找到第一個房間，下次不用試樓上及大字版了吧？」你們只測過第一條路線。哪個回應最好？

options.en: We seem on the right track, but let us test those routes and formats before extending the claim.
options.zh: 方向看來對了，但擴大結論前，先測那些路線及版本吧。

options.en: Use the first-room result as the upper-floor test too, since both are parts of the same guide.
options.zh: 既然屬於同一份指南，就把第一個房間的結果也當作樓上的測試吧。

options.en: Let us test the upper-floor directions only with staff who already know the building.
options.zh: 樓上的指示只讓已熟悉大樓的職員試用吧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 首條路線的試用結果值得保留，但不能代替樓上及大字版的測試。熟路職員的經驗，也不能完全代表初訪者怎樣使用指示。

speaking.en: We seem on the right track, but I want to explain the evidence and check what has not yet been tried.
speaking.zh: 方向看來對了，但我想交代根據，也核對還未試過的部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把有希望的方向與已完成成果分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友邀你參加比賽，說贏獎才表示寫作方向對了；你原來的目標卻是寫信跟祖母分享她熟悉的街坊故事，祖母已回信說認出其中兩位人物。用一至兩句英文說明自己判方向的根據，並尊重朋友重視比賽。

examples.en: I may be on the right track for my own aim, because Grandma recognised the neighbours and wrote back about them. The competition could matter to you, but sharing these stories with her is the result I am working towards.
examples.zh: 對我自己的目標而言，我可能方向對了，因為祖母認出那些鄰居，並回信談他們。比賽對你來說可能很重要，但跟她分享這些故事，才是我正努力爭取的成果。

examples.en: For me, being on the right track means the letters are helping Grandma and me exchange those memories. I respect your interest in the prize, but her reply gives me a different way to judge my progress.
examples.zh: 對我而言，方向合適是指信件正幫助祖母與我交流那些回憶。我尊重你對獎項的興趣，但她的回信給了我另一種判斷進展的依據。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用自己的分享目標及祖母的實際回信判斷方向，也尊重不同目標；不把個人有意義的進展說成已確定得獎。

takeaways.en: Her first clear explanation suggested she was on the right track, though the final comparison still needed work.
takeaways.zh: 她第一次清楚解釋，顯示方向對了，但最後的比較仍需要修改。

takeaways.en: We asked the participants what helped them before deciding whether the new format was on the right track.
takeaways.zh: 判斷新形式的方向是否合適前，我們先問參加者哪些部分有幫助。

lessons.titleEn: keep my eye on the ball

target.pattern: \bkeep(?:s|ing)? (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) eye on the ball\b|\bkept (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) eye on the ball\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A weekly budget helps me keep my eye on the ball.
sources.expression: keep my eye on the ball

brief.meaningEn: Stay focused on the important aim or responsibility rather than be distracted.
brief.meaningZh: 保持專注於重要目標或責任，不因其他事情而分心。
brief.grammar: keep/kept/keeping one’s eye on the ball; possessive matches the person focusing. Distinguish keep an eye on something, which more generally means monitor it.
brief.register: Informal sports idiom applied to practical concentration. It can encourage attention without implying every other need is irrelevant.
brief.boundaryZh: 專注不等於忽略協作、休息或新的重要資料；需要說清哪項責任是眼前重點。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不一定真有球賽，也不是只盯着一個物件，而沒有理解目的。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出主要任務，提醒或協商分工以免被次要事情帶走。

listening.promptZh: 這次的重點及處理先後是甚麼？

options.en: Agreement and questions needed attention before the poster-colour decision.
options.zh: 先處理受訪者的同意及訪問問題，再決定海報顏色。

options.en: The speaker had authorised the group to publish anything without checking the questions.
options.zh: 受訪者已准許小組不用核對問題，就公開任何內容。

options.en: Poster colours were the only issue the interview required.
options.zh: 海報顏色是訪問唯一需處理的事。

options.en: The poster had to be finished before the speaker could be asked about the questions.
options.zh: 海報需要先完成，才可以向受訪者詢問訪問問題。

listening.explanationZh: 工作有先後次序，並沒有取消海報，也沒有跳過受訪者的同意及問題。
listening.en: We needed to keep our eye on the ball during the interview preparations: confirming the speaker’s agreement and questions came before choosing the poster colours, though the poster still needed finishing later.
listening.zh: 準備訪問時，我們需要專注重點：先確認受訪者的同意及問題，再選海報顏色，雖然海報之後仍需要完成。

reply.promptEn: Why did you put the poster colours aside for the moment?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼暫把海報顏色放一旁？

options.en: We still needed to agree the interview and questions with the speaker.
options.zh: 我們仍需要跟受訪者議定訪問安排及問題。

options.en: Choosing colours could wait until those more important preparations were settled.
options.zh: 那些較重要的準備定好後，顏色可以稍後再選。

options.en: Keeping our eye on the ball meant attending to the interview’s purpose first.
options.zh: 保持專注，表示先照顧訪問的主要目的。

options.en: We did not want the visual details to distract us from the agreement needed for the conversation.
options.zh: 我們不想讓視覺細節，令大家忘記訪談所需的同意。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以訪問的主要責任，解釋暫緩選顏色的原因，不把專注當成取消其他工作。

scene.promptZh: 球隊正練接球，教練只叫球員看清來球，不談其他責任或計劃；你要分清此刻的字面指示。哪句準確？

options.en: Here, watching the ball is a literal instruction, rather than necessarily an idiom about the project’s priorities.
options.zh: 這裏看球是字面指示，不一定是指項目重點的慣用語。

options.en: The coach is talking about winning the season, rather than following the incoming ball.
options.zh: 教練在談贏今季比賽，不是看清投來的球。

options.en: The instruction asks the team to divide its training responsibilities.
options.zh: 指示要求球隊分配訓練職責。

scene.explanationZh: 需要按球賽當下的情況分清字面與比喻意思；這裏只要求看清來球，不應補上其他工作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只由 keep your eye on the ball 的比喻推出？

options.en: Focus on the important responsibility.
options.zh: 專注重要責任。

options.en: Ignore any new information even if it changes what the task requires.
options.zh: 即使新資料改變任務要求，也一概忽略。

options.en: Check what matters most for the present aim.
options.zh: 核對眼前目標最重要的是甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 專注於目標也需回應相關新資料，不等於拒絕調整。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「我們先把海報所有顏色配好，訪問問題等受訪者到了再想吧？」你尚未跟對方核對問題。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Let us keep our eye on the ball and agree the questions first; we can return to the colours afterwards.
options.zh: 先專注重點，議定問題；之後可再選顏色。

options.en: Our own outline looks complete, so I think we can settle the questions without contacting the speaker first.
options.zh: 我們自己的提綱看來完整，所以我想不用先聯絡受訪者，就可以定下問題。

options.en: I would wait until the speaker arrives to ask what topics they are willing to discuss, so we can avoid revising our outline beforehand.
options.zh: 我會等受訪者到場，才問他願意談哪些題目，這樣就不用事前修改提綱。

dialogue.explanationZh: 眼前責任是先跟受訪者確認意願及問題。提綱看來完整，不表示已得到對方確認；等到現場才問，也會失去事前協調的機會。

speaking.en: I need to keep my eye on the ball while still noticing information that changes what the task requires.
speaking.zh: 我需要專注重點，同時留意會改變任務要求的資料。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說主要責任及哪些新資訊仍需留意。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原本負責帶領社區步行導賞，出發前接到家人來電，說需要你陪他去處理一件急事。另一位導賞員熟悉路線，但還未知道集合人數及一處封路。你想專注於眼前的責任，先清楚交接並問他能否接手，再決定能否離開，不自行假定有人已接任。用一至兩句英文向他提出安排。

examples.en: I need to keep my eye on the ball by handing over the group properly before leaving for the family matter. Could I explain the headcount and closed path, then ask whether you can take over?
examples.zh: 處理家事離開之前，我需要專注眼前責任，把小組妥善交接。我可否先交代人數及封閉的步道，再問你能否接手？

examples.en: Let us keep our eye on the ball: the walkers need to know who is leading them and which route is open. Before I leave, can we check those details and agree whether you are able to lead?
examples.zh: 我們先專注眼前責任：參加者需要知道由誰帶領，以及哪條路可以走。離開之前，我們可否核對那些細節，並確認你能否帶隊？

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代帶隊責任所需的人數、路線及接任確認，再協商是否離開；不因自己有急事就假定交接完成，也不要求對方必須答應。

takeaways.en: She kept her eye on the ball by finishing the promised translation before redesigning the title page.
takeaways.zh: 她先完成答應的翻譯，再修改標題頁，藉此保持專注。

takeaways.en: We were keeping our eye on the ball when we asked whether the new suggestion helped the readers we were writing for.
takeaways.zh: 我們問新建議是否有助目標讀者，藉此保持專注。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Exercise can slide down the list when deadlines arrive.

brief.meaningEn: Become a lower priority as other matters receive attention first.
brief.meaningZh: 其他事情先獲注意時，某件事的優先程度下降。
brief.grammar: X slides/slid/is sliding down the list; list can be a metaphor for priorities rather than a written document. Distinguish lower priority from cancellation.
brief.register: Productive priority-position metaphor, not an assertion about an item moving physically.
brief.boundaryZh: 往後移不等於已取消或不再重視；需要看哪些事情獲先處理，以及是否仍有安排。
brief.misconceptionZh: 紙上的實際行序與優先程度下降，是兩回事；不能從比喻推斷每項工作的確切排名。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出優先下降的事及原因，協商如何重新給它位置。

listening.promptZh: 探訪目前是甚麼狀態？

options.en: Other work received attention first, while the postponed visit still mattered and lacked a new date.
options.zh: 其他工作先獲注意，延後的探訪仍重要，但未有新日期。

options.en: The team had cancelled the interview because nobody wanted the stories anymore.
options.zh: 小組已取消訪問，因為沒有人再想聽故事。

options.en: The postponed visit had already taken place before the costumes needed repair.
options.zh: 戲服需要修補之前，那次延後的探訪已完成。

options.en: A new interview date had been confirmed as soon as Tuesday was postponed.
options.zh: 星期二的探訪一延後，新日期就已經確定。

listening.explanationZh: 其他急事先獲處理，但小組並沒有取消探訪的意願。目前缺的是新日期，不是已完成探訪或已重新約定。
listening.en: The oral-history visit slid down the list when urgent costume repairs arrived; we still wanted to hear Mrs Chan’s stories, but had not agreed a new date after postponing Tuesday.
listening.zh: 戲服急需修補時，口述歷史探訪的優先次序往後移；我們仍想聽陳太的故事，但延後星期二的探訪後，還未議定新日期。

reply.promptEn: Why has the visit not yet been rearranged?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼探訪還未重新安排？

options.en: Urgent repairs took attention before we returned to choosing a date.
options.zh: 我們還未回到選日期的工作，就先處理急需修補的戲服。

options.en: The visit slid down the list when the costume work became urgent.
options.zh: 戲服工作變急時，探訪的優先次序往後移。

options.en: We postponed Tuesday and then dealt with the repairs first.
options.zh: 延後星期二的探訪後，我們先處理修補工作。

options.en: We still wanted the conversation, but had not made time to agree its new slot.
options.zh: 我們仍想談，但還未抽時間議定新時段。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋了暫未重新約定的優先次序，不把延後說成不在乎或已取消。

scene.promptZh: 故事裏，編輯把安全檢查那一行移到紙本清單最下方，卻仍規定要在其他事情前先完成。你要判斷的是實際優先次序。哪句最好？

options.en: Its position on the page changed, but the instructions still give the check first priority.
options.zh: 紙上位置改了，但指示仍把檢查列為首要工作。

options.en: Moving the line down establishes that the check is now less urgent than every other task.
options.zh: 把一行移低，就確立檢查現在比其他每件事都不急。

options.en: The editor removed the check from the instructions instead of moving its line.
options.zh: 編輯從指示中刪掉了檢查，而不只是移動行序。

scene.explanationZh: 紙上位置不能代替實際要求；這裏仍規定先做檢查，也沒有把它刪掉。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「The visit slid down the list」推出？

options.en: It received less immediate priority.
options.zh: 它較少獲即時優先處理。

options.en: The visit was definitely cancelled and no longer mattered.
options.zh: 探訪肯定已取消，也不再重要。

options.en: The context can identify what was dealt with first.
options.zh: 情境可指出先處理了甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 降低優先次序不自動等於取消或不重視，需看後續安排。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「探訪延後了，等所有戲服事都沒疑問才聯絡陳太吧？」你們尚未重約，也不知她之後時間。哪句最好？

options.en: It has slid down the list, but we can contact Mrs Chan now to ask about dates while the repairs continue.
options.zh: 探訪的優先次序已往後移，但修補繼續進行時，仍可以現在聯絡陳太，詢問日期。

options.en: Let us wait until every repair is finished before telling her whether we still want the visit.
options.zh: 等所有修補完成後，才告訴她是否仍想探訪。

options.en: Choose a new date ourselves and send it as fixed without asking when she is available.
options.zh: 自己選一個新日子，當作已定案發給她，不用問她何時有空。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以把聯絡重新納入當下分工，同時尊重受訪者的時間；不需要等所有工作完成，也不能自行替對方定日期。

speaking.en: It slid down the list when other work became urgent, but I still want to agree a time for it.
speaking.zh: 其他工作變得緊急時，它的優先次序往後移，但我仍想為它議定一個時段。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分降低優先程度與取消。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你想在小說中寫一個角色長期把給舊同學的信往後拖，並非不想聯絡。今天他在一張紙背看見未寄地址，決定先寫兩句，不再等整晚有空。用一至兩句英文寫實際旁白，讓讀者看出優先下降及新的小動作。

examples.en: The letter had slid down the list as other tasks filled his evenings, though he still wanted to write. When he found the address on the back of the page, he turned it over and began with two lines.
examples.zh: 其他工作佔滿他的晚上，那封信的優先次序一直往後移，但他仍想寫。在紙背看見地址時，他把紙翻過來，先寫兩句。

examples.en: Writing to his old classmate kept sliding down the list while he waited for a completely free evening. This time he put the address beside his cup and wrote the first two sentences before opening another task.
examples.zh: 他一直等一個完全空閒的晚上，給舊同學寫信便不斷往後移。這次他把地址放在杯子旁，開始另一項工作前先寫兩句。

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出具體旁白及重新開始的動作，分清仍想聯絡與一直延後；不因未寄信，就斷定人物沒有感情。

takeaways.en: The optional illustration slid down the list when the writer needed to check the missing quotation first.
takeaways.zh: 作者需要先核對遺漏的引文時，選做插圖的優先次序往後移。

takeaways.en: She noticed her own question sliding down the list and asked the group to leave time for it at the next meeting.
takeaways.zh: 她留意到自己的問題一直往後移，便請小組在下次開會時預留時間。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: I had planned to start, but I made a whole week of excuses.

brief.meaningEn: A sustained period of giving reasons for not doing something, presented by the speaker as avoidant excuses.
brief.meaningZh: 說話者把一段持續提出不做某事的理由，形容為一整星期找藉口。
brief.grammar: a whole week of excuses; whole stresses the extent, while of excuses characterises that period. It is not a separate fixed idiom; whether a reason is an excuse depends on context.
brief.register: Natural emphatic spoken phrase, often self-critical. Do not label another person’s genuine obstacles excuses without evidence.
brief.boundaryZh: 不能只因事情未做，就判定理由虛假；whole week 可以加強語氣，精確天數需要另有記錄。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要分清承認自己迴避，與替別人下懶惰的判斷；實際障礙仍可能需要處理。
brief.outcomeZh: 能坦白說自己延後的行為，提出第一步而不一概否定所有理由。

listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣理解自己的延後？

options.en: Choosing a notebook had become a way to postpone opening files that were already available.
options.zh: 選筆記簿成了延後打開已有檔案的方法。

options.en: The only copy of the interview files was missing, so the speaker could not begin.
options.zh: 訪問檔案的唯一副本已遺失，所以說話者無法開始。

options.en: The first recording had already been labelled before the week of delays.
options.zh: 延後一周之前，第一段錄音的標記工作已完成。

options.en: The speaker planned to buy stationery before making any start today.
options.zh: 說話者今天仍計劃先買文具，才開始。

listening.explanationZh: 說話者承認檔案可用，卻用選文具來延後工作；今天是先標記錄音，而不是檔案缺失或工作已完成。
listening.en: I had a whole week of excuses for not opening the old interview files: I kept saying I needed a better notebook, though the files were already on my laptop; today I will label the first recording before choosing any stationery.
listening.zh: 我一整星期找理由不開舊訪問檔案，一直說需要更好的筆記簿，但檔案其實已在電腦裏。今天我會先標記第一段錄音，再選文具。

reply.promptEn: Why will you label one recording before choosing stationery?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼先標一段錄音，才選文具？

options.en: I want to stop using the notebook choice to postpone the work.
options.zh: 我想停止用選筆記簿來延後工作。

options.en: The files are available, so the first label does not need a new notebook.
options.zh: 檔案可用，開始做第一項標記並不需要新筆記簿。

options.en: After a whole week of excuses, I want a concrete start on the files.
options.zh: 整星期找藉口後，我想實際開始處理檔案。

options.en: Starting with one recording would address what I had kept avoiding.
options.zh: 由一段錄音開始，可處理自己一直迴避的事。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以自己可以做的步驟回應延後，不用自責代替實際開始。

scene.promptZh: 同學尚未交錄音，因學校借的設備壞了，已聯絡職員並約替代設備；你沒有資料顯示她在迴避。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The account identifies an equipment problem and a response to it, not enough evidence to call it a week of excuses.
options.zh: 敘述有設備問題及處理行動，還不足以稱為整星期找藉口。

options.en: She postponed the recording simply to avoid speaking, rather than because the borrowed device failed.
options.zh: 她只是為了避免開口錄音才延後，而不是因為借來的設備故障。

options.en: She has waited without asking about a replacement device.
options.zh: 她一直在等，沒有詢問替代設備。

scene.explanationZh: 已知資料包括設備故障及她聯絡職員的行動，不能只因遲交，就改說她在逃避錄音；也不能說她沒有詢問替代設備。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由 a whole week of excuses 得出？

options.en: The speaker presents repeated reasons as avoidant.
options.zh: 說話者把反覆理由呈現為迴避。

options.en: Every obstacle faced by anyone involved was necessarily invented.
options.zh: 每個相關人士面對的所有障礙，必定都是編造的。

options.en: Whole adds emphasis to the described period.
options.zh: whole 加強對該段時間的強調。

contrast.explanationZh: 這是敘述者的評價及時間上的強調，不足以判定所有人的每項障礙都是虛假的。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友問：「你說自己一周找藉口，是不是新筆記簿真的必須先買？」你已可直接在現有檔案寫標記。哪句最好？

options.en: No, it was a whole week of excuses; I can label the recording now and choose a notebook later.
options.zh: 不是，那是一整星期找藉口；我現在就可以標記錄音，筆記簿稍後再選。

options.en: I should compare more notebook covers before testing whether I can label the file.
options.zh: 我應先比較更多筆記簿封面，才試試能否標記檔案。

options.en: Let us plan the stationery trip first and leave the available recordings until another week.
options.zh: 先計劃買文具，把已有錄音再放另一周吧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接說明文具不是開始工作的必要條件；繼續選封面或先安排購物，會延續同樣的迴避。

speaking.en: I called it a whole week of excuses because I had a way to begin but kept postponing that first step.
speaking.zh: 我稱那是一整星期找藉口，因為明明有方法開始，卻一直延後第一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分自我承認迴避與有根據的實際障礙。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你答應替朋友修一句故事開頭，自己卻因怕提出不同看法而拖了一周，總說「再看一次」。朋友現在以為你根本不喜歡她的作品。用一至兩句英文道歉，承認自己的迴避，並先徵詢她是否仍想聽具體建議。

examples.en: I am sorry for a whole week of excuses about rereading; I was avoiding saying that I read the opening differently, not rejecting your story. Would you still like me to explain one suggestion?
examples.zh: 對不起，我整星期用重讀來找藉口；我是在迴避說出自己對開頭的不同理解，而不是否定你的故事。你還想聽我解釋一項建議嗎？

examples.en: You deserved an answer instead of a whole week of excuses. I was nervous about disagreeing, and I would like to ask whether you still want my comment before I send it.
examples.zh: 你值得得到回答，而不是一整星期的藉口。我是害怕意見不同，所以發出意見前，想先問你現在還想不想聽。

writing.selfCheckZh: 實際道歉，承認自己因害怕意見不同而迴避，並詢問朋友是否仍願意聽；不把道歉當成對方必須接受意見，或已經原諒自己。

takeaways.en: A whole week of excuses ended when he admitted he was unsure how to ask the archive for help.
takeaways.zh: 他承認不知道怎樣向檔案室求助後，終於結束了一整星期的藉口。

takeaways.en: She apologised for a whole week of excuses and asked whether the promised feedback was still wanted.
takeaways.zh: 她為整星期找藉口道歉，並問對方是否仍想要答應的回饋。

lessons.titleZh: 像攀山般逐步克服困難

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Learning a language can feel like climbing a mountain.

brief.meaningEn: Work towards a demanding goal, pictured as an ascent that takes stages and sustained effort.
brief.meaningZh: 把朝困難目標努力，比作需要分階段、持續付出的攀登。
brief.grammar: learning/finishing X is like climbing a mountain; distinguish a metaphor about difficulty and stages from a literal climbing journey. Not every step must feel steadily easier.
brief.register: Productive goal-as-mountain comparison, rather than a unique dictionary idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 有困難不等於不能完成，也不保證努力便一定到頂；可有休息、支援及回頭重試。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能從比喻推斷真的有山，或每個人都需要同一路線；這也不同於把小事誇大的另一個山岳意象。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體階段解釋困難，描述進展及所獲支援。

listening.promptZh: 攀山意象主要說明甚麼？

options.en: A demanding learning process with useful smaller gains and unresolved parts.
options.zh: 這是一段有小收穫、卻仍有未解部分的困難學習過程。

options.en: The main difficulty was finding where the letters were stored, rather than learning to read their handwriting.
options.zh: 主要困難是找出信件存放在哪裏，而不是學習辨認手寫字。

options.en: The complete letters had become easy as soon as one name was recognised.
options.zh: 一認出名字，所有信就已經容易閱讀。

options.en: The archive notes had replaced the need to look at the handwriting.
options.zh: 檔案筆記已取代閱讀手寫文字的需要。

listening.explanationZh: 認出名字只是其中一步，整句仍需要耐心比較。困難在於閱讀手寫文字，不是尋找信件存放位置，也不是所有句子已讀懂或只需看筆記。
listening.en: Learning to read the old handwritten letters felt like climbing a mountain: recognising each name helped, but whole sentences still took patient comparison with the archive notes, and some pages remained unclear.
listening.zh: 學習閱讀舊手寫信像攀山：認出每個名字都有幫助，但整句仍需要耐心跟檔案筆記比較，部分頁面依然不清楚。

reply.promptEn: Why do you compare reading the letters to a difficult ascent?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼把讀信比作艱難攀登？

options.en: I made smaller gains but still had to work carefully on whole sentences.
options.zh: 我有小進展，卻仍需要仔細處理整句。

options.en: Some pages remained hard despite recognising individual names.
options.zh: 雖然認出個別名字，部分頁面仍然難讀。

options.en: It felt like climbing a mountain because understanding came through several demanding stages.
options.zh: 理解需要經過幾個費力的階段，所以感覺像攀山。

options.en: The comparison captures the effort between the first recognisable details and a fuller reading.
options.zh: 這個比喻呈現了從認得最初細節，到較完整閱讀之間所需的努力。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以學習閱讀的過程及分階段難度作根據，不把小進展當成所有困難已解決。

scene.promptZh: 故事人物正在真山路一步步向上走，旁白只記實際行程，沒有拿它比學習。哪句最準確？

options.en: Climbing a mountain is literal in this passage; a broader goal metaphor would need more context.
options.zh: 這段攀山是字面的行程；若把它理解為較廣泛目標的比喻，需要更多情境。

options.en: The passage establishes that the walker is studying handwritten letters rather than travelling.
options.zh: 段落確立了行人正在讀手寫信，而不是出行。

options.en: The words describe how quickly a simple task was finished, not an ascent.
options.zh: 字句描述簡單任務很快完成，不是攀登。

scene.explanationZh: 同一組字詞也可以真的描寫山路，不應因本課有比喻，就把每次攀山都解作學習。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「Learning felt like climbing a mountain」推出？

options.en: Learning felt demanding and extended.
options.zh: 學習感覺費力且需持續。

options.en: The learner is guaranteed to finish if they never take a break.
options.zh: 只要永不休息，學員便獲保證完成。

options.en: The speaker can explain which smaller steps helped.
options.zh: 說話者可解釋哪些小步有幫助。

contrast.explanationZh: 攀山意象不提供成功保證，也沒有要求不停歇；需要按具體過程說明難度。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「認到名字，就可以把所有頁面標成已讀懂了吧？」你仍有整句未看清。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It still feels like climbing a mountain; the names help, but let us mark which sentences remain uncertain.
options.zh: 這仍像攀山；名字有幫助，但先標出哪些句子還不確定吧。

options.en: Use the clear names as our evidence for the unclear sentences too.
options.zh: 也用已看清楚的名字，作為理解未清楚句子的證據。

options.en: We should spend the next session copying only the names again rather than examining any sentence.
options.zh: 下次應該只再抄名字，不看任何句子。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以利用小進展繼續處理難處，但認得名字不能代替理解整句的證據；只重複已認出的部分，也未對準下一個需要。

speaking.en: Learning it felt like climbing a mountain, with small gains that helped me face the parts I still could not understand.
speaking.zh: 學習它像攀山，小進展幫我面對仍不明白的部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以實際階段說困難，不把比喻當成功保證。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在社區故事集完成後致謝。你覺得整個計劃像攀山，但不想把自己寫成獨力英雄；鄰居借出照片，伙伴聽錄音找漏句，大家也按需要停下重聽。用一至兩句英文寫實際致謝，承認共同支援。

examples.en: Making this collection felt like climbing a mountain, but I did not make the journey alone. Thank you for lending photographs and listening again when we needed to find a missing line.
examples.zh: 製作故事集像攀山，但我不是獨自走這段路。謝謝大家借出照片，也在我們需要找漏句時再聽一遍。

examples.en: We were climbing a mountain together as we gathered these stories, and the finished book carries more than my work. I am grateful to the neighbours who shared photographs and the partners who made time to listen with me.
examples.zh: 收集故事時，我們像一起攀山，完成的書不只承載我的工作。我感謝分享照片的鄰居，以及預留時間陪我聽錄音的伙伴。

glossary.en: made time to listen with me

writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出實際致謝及他人的具體貢獻，保留困難旅程的意象，不把成果全歸自己，也不把停下重聽視為失敗。

takeaways.en: Writing the first chapter was like climbing a mountain, though a friend’s questions helped her find the next foothold.
takeaways.zh: 寫第一章像攀山，但朋友的問題幫她找到下一個落腳處。

takeaways.en: They had climbed a mountain to finish the archive, and the final page listed everyone whose patient help had made it possible.
takeaways.zh: 完成檔案像攀完一座山，最後一頁列出每位耐心幫忙、促成成果的人。

lessons.titleZh: 把事情安排妥當，認真落實

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: I need to get my act together before the exam.

brief.meaningEn: Become organised enough to act effectively or deal responsibly with what needs doing.
brief.meaningZh: 做事變得較有條理，以便有效行動，或妥善處理需要做的事。
brief.grammar: get/got/getting one’s act together; possessive matches the person. Describe practical organisation, not literal theatre acting. Often used about oneself; telling another person to do it can sound critical.
brief.register: Informal idiom, sometimes impatient or self-critical. It need not imply moral worth, perfection or a permanent transformation.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是從此不會犯錯，也不只是大家一起演戲；需要指出文件、安排或承諾如何改善。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以承認安排上的失誤，而不把人一概判為沒用；結果仍可能需要檢查。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說清自己需要整理的事情，為失誤負責，並提出可行安排。

listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣回應組織問題？

options.en: Set up a shared location and internal dates to distinguish the drafts after sending confusing versions.
options.zh: 發出混亂版本後，用共用位置及檔案內的日期分清初稿。

options.en: Treat the most recently sent file as the only reference without keeping a dated copy.
options.zh: 把最近發出的檔案當作唯一參考，不保留註有日期的副本。

options.en: Leave the partner to identify the current draft without clarifying the versions.
options.zh: 沒有澄清版本，就留伙伴自行辨認現行初稿。

options.en: Rename the files again without agreeing which folder the partner should use.
options.zh: 再改檔名，卻沒有議定伙伴應使用哪個資料夾。

listening.explanationZh: 共用位置及日期是具體的整理方法，不是只靠發送先後、讓別人猜版本，或只是再次改名。
listening.en: I needed to get my act together before the next edit: I had sent two differently named drafts to the same partner, so I agreed one shared folder and wrote the version date inside each file.
listening.zh: 下次編稿前，我需要把事情安排妥當：我曾把兩份名字不同的初稿發給同一位伙伴，所以我們議定一個共用資料夾，並在每份檔案內寫上版本日期。

reply.promptEn: Why did you agree a shared folder and add version dates?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼議定共用資料夾，並加上版本日期？

options.en: My partner had received two drafts that were difficult to distinguish.
options.zh: 伙伴收到兩個難分清的初稿。

options.en: I needed to get my act together so the next edit used a clear version.
options.zh: 我需要把事情安排妥當，讓下次編稿有清楚的版本可用。

options.en: The earlier file names had not made our working copy clear.
options.zh: 先前的檔名沒有說清楚，哪份才是工作版本。

options.en: We needed one agreed place and information that would identify each draft.
options.zh: 我們需要一個議定位置，以及能辨認每份初稿的資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以曾經出現的版本混亂，解釋具體整理的需要，不把改名本身當作已經清楚。

scene.promptZh: 故事中三位義工答應帶展覽用品，卻尚未分誰帶哪件；沒有任何舞台演出。他們說需 get our act together，哪句最準確？

options.en: They need to get their act together by agreeing who brings each item.
options.zh: 他們需要議定誰帶哪件用品，把事情安排妥當。

options.en: They are asking for another performer to complete the cast for a joint scene.
options.zh: 他們在找另一演員，湊齊共同演出的人手。

options.en: The item responsibilities are already settled, and only the wording of the announcement remains.
options.zh: 用品分工已定，只剩公告字句待改。

scene.explanationZh: 這裏是要安排尚未分配的責任，不是湊齊演員，也沒有資料顯示分工已定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「I got my act together」推出？

options.en: The speaker became better organised for something that needed doing.
options.zh: 說話者在處理需要做的事情時，變得較有條理。

options.en: The speaker will never make another mistake in any task.
options.zh: 說話者今後做任何事都永不再錯。

options.en: The context can give concrete changes to arrangements.
options.zh: 情境可交代安排的具體改變。

contrast.explanationZh: 改善安排，不表示從此永遠完美；需要按實際任務看後續表現。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「下次再換新檔名，應不用議共用位置吧？」你們之前已因版本不清浪費時間。哪句最好？

options.en: I need to get my act together by agreeing where we work and marking the dates, not just inventing another name.
options.zh: 我需要議定工作位置，並標上日期，把事情安排妥當，而不只是另想一個名字。

options.en: Let us keep separate private folders and ask you to guess which draft I mean.
options.zh: 各自保留私人資料夾，請你猜我指哪份稿吧。

options.en: Choose the newest-looking file name each time without checking its contents or date.
options.zh: 每次選看來最新的檔名，不用核對內容或日期。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要對準已知的版本問題，議定來源及識別資料；分散存放或猜檔名，都沒有解決它。

speaking.en: I need to get my act together, so I will make the arrangement clear and check that I have done what I promised.
speaking.zh: 我需要把事情安排妥當，所以會說清楚安排，也核對自己是否完成答應的事。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把自我要求落在具體可行的行動上。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你兩次答應還朋友一本用來備課的書，卻都沒帶。你想道歉，不說朋友催得太多；你願今天確認交收地方，出門前把書放袋，並問她是否已需改用另一份資料。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: I need to get my act together about returning your book, and I am sorry I forgot it twice. Could we confirm where to meet today, and have you already needed to use another source for the lesson?
examples.zh: 還書這件事，我需要認真安排；兩次忘帶，我很抱歉。我們可以確認今天在哪裏交收嗎？也想問你是否已需要改用另一份備課資料。

examples.en: I have not followed through on bringing the book, so I need to get my act together rather than ask you to keep reminding me. I will put it in my bag before leaving; please tell me where you can collect it and whether the delay has changed your preparation.
examples.zh: 我沒有做到帶書，所以需要把事情安排妥當，而不應要你一直提醒。出門前我會把書放進袋裏；請告訴我哪裏方便交收，也讓我知道延誤是否影響了你的準備。

writing.selfCheckZh: 實際道歉，承擔忘記還書的責任，提出交收及出門前的安排，也詢問對方受影響的情況；不把承諾當作已還書，也不責怪提醒。

takeaways.en: She got her act together by checking the promised tasks with her partner before accepting another one.
takeaways.zh: 接受另一項工作前，她先跟伙伴核對答應的任務，讓自己做事更有條理。

takeaways.en: He was getting his act together for the exhibition, but still asked a colleague to check the final labels.
takeaways.zh: 他正把事情安排妥當，準備展覽，但仍請同事核對最後的標籤。

sources.sentence: Completing one small task is a way of building momentum.

sources.sentence: Joint projects can gather real momentum.

brief.meaningEn: Develop progress or participation that helps further progress become easier or more likely.
brief.meaningZh: 累積進展或參與，讓之後的進展更容易繼續。
brief.grammar: build momentum / gather momentum; both describe progress that makes further progress more likely. Real intensifies the degree but is optional.
brief.register: Conventional motion metaphor, also a natural collocation. Identify the actual sequence linking early and later action.
brief.boundaryZh: 忙碌或速度快，不一定表示正朝目標前進；勢頭不保證完成，休息也不自動等於前功盡棄。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需要說明小進展如何支持後續，而不只是列出很多不相關工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述進展之間的連繫及下一個需要，並保留暫停或調整的空間。

listening.promptZh: 最初的進展怎樣支持之後的工作？

options.en: An answer led to a follow-up, which helped identify an example and brought another contribution.
options.zh: 回答引出追問，幫忙找出需要補充例子的地方，再帶來另一項貢獻。

options.en: The guide was complete before the first question, with no changes arising from it.
options.zh: 第一條問題提出前，指南已完成，問題沒有帶來改動。

options.en: The team became busier by taking unrelated orders instead of improving the guide.
options.zh: 小組接了不相關的訂單，變得更忙，卻沒有改善指南。

options.en: The final route had been checked before the readers offered any questions or maps.
options.zh: 讀者提出問題或地圖之前，最後一段路線已核對妥當。

listening.explanationZh: 一項回應連到下一項具體幫助，才顯示推進的勢頭；路線仍待核對，不是所有工作已完成。
listening.en: Answering one newcomer’s question helped us build momentum on the guide: her follow-up revealed a missing example, and another reader then offered a clearer map, though the final route still needed checking.
listening.zh: 回答一位新來者的問題，幫助我們逐步推進指南：她的追問揭示缺少一個例子，另一位讀者再提供較清楚的地圖，但最後一段路線仍待核對。

reply.promptEn: Why did the first question help the guide project progress?
reply.promptZh: 第一條問題為甚麼有助指南項目推進？

options.en: It opened a follow-up that showed us what example was missing.
options.zh: 它引出追問，顯示缺少哪個例子。

options.en: The exchange brought useful information and encouraged another reader to contribute.
options.zh: 交流帶來有用資料，也促成另一位讀者的貢獻。

options.en: We began building momentum as one answer led to another useful step.
options.zh: 一個回答引出下一個有用步驟，我們便開始累積勢頭。

options.en: The early conversation gave later work a more specific direction.
options.zh: 最初的談話，讓之後的工作有較具體方向。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用回應與下一步之間的連繫解釋勢頭，不只是說事情變多，也不保證已能完工。

scene.promptZh: 小組一晚不停換封面字體，卻沒處理讀者仍找不到的入口資料；他們只以按鍵次數說項目勢頭很好。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Many design changes do not by themselves show that the group is building momentum towards a usable guide.
options.zh: 設計改動多，本身不足以顯示小組正朝可用指南的目標累積勢頭。

options.en: The group revised the entrance directions during the same evening, not just the cover typefaces.
options.zh: 小組在同一晚也修訂了入口指示，而不只是更換封面字體。

options.en: Because the team was busy, no further check of the reader’s problem is needed.
options.zh: 小組很忙，所以不用再核對讀者的問題。

scene.explanationZh: 改動字體可能很忙碌，但不能代替處理入口資料。敘述沒有說入口指示已修訂，仍需按讀者的實際問題判斷進展。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「We are building momentum」推出？

options.en: Early progress is helping further action develop.
options.zh: 較早的進展，正在幫助後續行動發展。

options.en: Taking a break will necessarily erase every earlier gain.
options.zh: 一休息便必定抹去所有已有收穫。

options.en: The speaker can describe how one action supported another.
options.zh: 說話者可以說明，一項行動如何支持另一項。

contrast.explanationZh: 形成勢頭，不表示必須不停工作，也不保證暫停後，已學會或已完成的事情全部消失。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「開始有人提供地圖，已可不用試最後路線了吧？」那段仍未核。哪句最好？

options.en: We are building momentum, and checking that route is the next useful step rather than something the enthusiasm replaces.
options.zh: 我們正累積勢頭，核對那段路線是下一個有用步驟，不是熱情可以取代的事情。

options.en: I think the clearer map already includes a test of the final route, rather than just a reader’s contribution.
options.zh: 我想那張較清楚的地圖已包括最後路線的測試，而不只是讀者提供的資料。

options.en: We should start a new map from nothing instead of examining what the reader has offered.
options.zh: 我們應從頭畫一張新地圖，而不是先查看讀者提供的內容。

dialogue.explanationZh: 讀者提供地圖，是可以利用的進展，但不等於路線已經試行。下一步可先查看這項貢獻並核實路線，不必直接丟開它重新開始。

speaking.en: We are building momentum when one useful step gives us information and support for the next one.
speaking.zh: 一個有用步驟為下一步提供資料及支援時，我們就在累積推進的勢頭。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用具體連繫說明進展，不只是計算有多忙。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：合唱小組完成第一段編曲後，因場地問題暫停兩周。伙伴擔心原有進展全沒了，想要求大家連夜補回。你想先確認大家仍記得哪些聲部，安排一次短重溫，再商量進度，不責怪任何人休息。用一至兩句英文提出重新開始的安排。

examples.en: We had begun building momentum before the room closed, and the arrangement we completed is still there to return to. Could we check which parts we remember in one short rehearsal before deciding how to continue?
examples.zh: 場地關閉前，我們已開始累積勢頭，完成的編曲仍在，可以回去接上。我們可否先用一次短排練，核對仍記得哪些聲部，再決定怎樣繼續？

examples.en: The break does not mean we must build momentum by working through the night. Let us begin with the section we finished, hear what needs revisiting and agree the next rehearsal together.
examples.zh: 暫停不表示要連夜工作來重建勢頭。先從已完成的那段開始，聽聽哪些地方需要重溫，再一起議定下次排練吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認活動曾暫停，也保留已完成的編曲；先核對記憶及重溫，再議定有範圍的安排，不假定全部忘記，也不要求補回所有時數。

takeaways.en: Finishing the first panel helped the painters build momentum as they could show volunteers exactly what needed doing next.
takeaways.zh: 完成第一幅畫板，讓畫師可以具體示範下一項工作，幫助他們累積勢頭。

takeaways.en: The repair campaign gathered real momentum once three local groups offered volunteers.
takeaways.zh: 三個本地團體提供義工後，維修倡議真正開始有勢頭。

sources.sentence: Life throws a few curveballs when plans seem settled.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Life sometimes throws a curveball despite careful plans.

sources.sentence: The project kept throwing curveballs at us.

brief.meaningEn: Present unexpected difficulties or challenges that complicate an intended course.
brief.meaningZh: 帶來意料外的困難或挑戰，讓原來的打算變得更複雜。
brief.grammar: throw a few curveballs / throw curveballs at someone; throw, throws, throwing, threw and thrown can frame unexpected complications, not literal baseball pitches. An unexpected curveball may name one unforeseen complication.
brief.register: Common informal baseball idiom, not a literal sports action in these examples.
brief.boundaryZh: 意外難題不表示整個計劃失敗，也未說每項困難都事先無法預知；需按實際預期說明。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能把已列明、已準備的普通工作一概叫作意外，也不能從意外推斷有人刻意搗亂。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出預期與突然出現的差別，描述回應或保留未知。

listening.promptZh: 哪兩項事情偏離原來預期？

options.en: The booked reader became unavailable, and unexpected letters arrived.
options.zh: 已約好的朗讀者不能來，並收到一批意料外的信件。

options.en: The team had planned both the reader’s absence and the extra box as regular programme items.
options.zh: 小組原已把朗讀者缺席及新箱信件列為正常環節。

options.en: The programme was completed before any new information appeared.
options.zh: 任何新資料出現前，節目已完成。

options.en: The reader arrived as booked, while the expected box failed to arrive.
options.zh: 朗讀者如約到場，原先期待的箱子卻沒有到。

listening.explanationZh: 兩件新事情改變了原來安排及資料範圍，小組仍需要重新決定；不是原已計劃，也不是事情剛好相反。
listening.en: The archive project threw us two curveballs: the reader we had booked was suddenly unavailable, and a box arrived with letters we had not known existed; we paused the programme to agree what needed a new decision.
listening.zh: 檔案項目給我們兩項意外難題：已約好的朗讀者突然不能來，另有一箱原先不知道存在的信送到。我們暫停定下節目，商量哪些事情需要重新決定。

reply.promptEn: Why did you pause the programme planning?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼暫停定下節目？

options.en: Our available reader and the material we could include had both changed unexpectedly.
options.zh: 可用的朗讀者，以及可以納入的資料，都意外改變了。

options.en: The project threw us two curveballs that needed fresh decisions.
options.zh: 項目帶來兩項需要重新決定的意外難題。

options.en: We needed to consider the new letters as well as the missing reader.
options.zh: 我們需要同時考慮新信件，以及缺席的朗讀者。

options.en: The original plan no longer covered all the information and people now involved.
options.zh: 原有安排未涵蓋現在的全部資料及人手。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體新情況，解釋重新商量的原因，不把意外當成全盤失敗。

scene.promptZh: 作坊介紹已說最後需自行演示，參加者讀過並選好演示題目；演示本身仍有難度，但沒有新要求出現。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The demonstration is a known challenge; it doesn't throw them an unexpected curveball because it was announced beforehand.
options.zh: 示範是已知的挑戰；它早已公布，不算突然給他們帶來意外難題。

options.en: A demanding task is necessarily a surprise even when it was explained and prepared for.
options.zh: 即使已解釋並準備，有難度的工作必定是意外。

options.en: The account says the demonstration was added only after they arrived.
options.zh: 敘述說他們到場後才新增示範。

scene.explanationZh: 要分清有難度與突如其來；已知要求，不會因為困難就變成沒有預告。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「Life threw us a curveball」推出？

options.en: Something unexpected complicated the situation.
options.zh: 意料外的事令情況更複雜。

options.en: Someone deliberately caused the difficulty to defeat the group.
options.zh: 有人刻意製造困難來擊敗小組。

options.en: The context can identify what had been expected instead.
options.zh: 情境可交代原本期待甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 意外本身不會提供惡意或造成者動機的證據，需要另有資料。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說：「箱裏的信件不在預期中，就一定不能放進節目，直接退回吧？」你們未查內容，也未問公開意願。哪個回應最好？

options.en: It has thrown us a curveball, but let us check the contents and permission before deciding what belongs in the programme.
options.zh: 它帶來意外難題，但先核對內容及許可，再決定甚麼可以放進節目吧。

options.en: Judge the new box only by whether its letters have the same dates as the ones we already selected.
options.zh: 只按新箱信件的日期，是否跟已選的信相同，來判斷它是否有用。

options.en: Put the letters straight into the public reading so the new box does not delay the plan.
options.zh: 直接把信放進公開朗讀，避免新箱信件延誤計劃。

dialogue.explanationZh: 意外資料需要按實際內容及公開意願考慮；日期是否相同，未足以判斷用途，也不能直接公開。

speaking.en: Life threw us a curveball, so we checked what had changed before deciding which part of the plan to revise.
speaking.zh: 生活帶來意外難題，所以我們先核對改變了甚麼，再決定調整哪部分計劃。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指出意外與原預期之間的差別。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說情節摘要。主角一直以為朋友沒回信，已打算結束來往；今天突然發現回信多年前被放進另一箱，信中卻留一個她不懂的問題。用一至兩句英文寫這個意外如何令她重新思考，不替她定朋友現在的意願。

examples.en: The old reply threw her a curveball just as she was ready to end the friendship. She now had to reconsider the silence and find out what the unanswered question had meant, without assuming she knew how her friend felt today.
examples.zh: 正想結束友誼時，舊回信帶來意外難題。她需要重新思考那段沉默，查明未回答的問題當年有甚麼意思，而不假定自己知道朋友今天的感受。

examples.en: Finding the mislaid letter threw her a curveball: the silence she had resented was no longer the whole story. The question at the end made her pause before deciding whether to contact her friend.
examples.zh: 找到放錯的信，帶來意外難題：她曾埋怨的沉默，不再是事情的全貌。末尾的問題，讓她在決定是否聯絡前停下來。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用實際舊信改變角色所知的前因，保留末尾問題及朋友現在意願仍未知的狀態；不把意外直接等同於復合或陰謀。

takeaways.en: The unexpected question threw the panel a curveball, and they asked for a moment to check the figures.
takeaways.zh: 意料外的問題令小組措手不及，他們請求一點時間核對數字。

takeaways.en: Each permit review threw curveballs at us, so we scheduled extra time for revisions.
takeaways.zh: 每次許可證審核都帶來意外難題，因此我們預留更多時間修改。

lessons.titleZh: 展現自己在困難中的為人或能力

target.pattern: \bwhat (?:I am|you are|he is|she is|we are|they are|I was|you were|he was|she was|we were|they were|someone is|my partner was) made of\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A difficult season can show what you are made of.

brief.meaningEn: The character, resolve or ability someone shows, especially when challenged.
brief.meaningZh: 某人在面對挑戰時展現的為人、意志或能力。
brief.grammar: show what someone is made of; embedded clause uses statement order. The literal material-composition meaning differs; actions in context support a limited judgement, not a complete permanent verdict about a person.
brief.register: Conventional character metaphor. Can praise persistence, patience or generosity, not only solo toughness.
brief.boundaryZh: 一段表現不能判定一個人的全部價值，也不表示不能求助或改變；需要有具體行為支持判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不把未成功直接判作沒有韌性；外在條件及支援，仍可能影響結果。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體行動說明所欣賞的表現，不要求人經痛苦來證明自己。

listening.promptZh: 說話者以甚麼行為支持這個評價？

options.en: Patience, practical help and asking for a pause instead of blaming a newcomer.
options.zh: 她有耐性、實際幫忙，並請求暫停，而不責怪新成員。

options.en: The partner proved she could complete every role alone without help.
options.zh: 伙伴證明了自己不用幫忙，也能獨自完成每個角色。

options.en: The newest member was found responsible and told to leave before reconstruction began.
options.zh: 重新整理前，發現新成員有責任，並叫他離開。

options.en: The partner refused to pause and insisted that the actors continue without cues.
options.zh: 伙伴拒絕暫停，堅持讓演員沒有提示也繼續。

listening.explanationZh: 具體證據是耐心協作及適時停下，不是獨力包辦、已判定新成員的責任，或拒絕暫停。
listening.en: The lost script showed me what my partner was made of: she stayed patient, helped each actor reconstruct a cue and asked for a pause when we needed it, rather than blaming the newest member.
listening.zh: 劇本遺失，讓我看見伙伴的為人：她保持耐性，幫每位演員重新整理接話提示，需要時請求暫停，而不是責怪最新加入的成員。

reply.promptEn: Why did that incident make you appreciate your partner?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼那次事件令你更欣賞伙伴？

options.en: She helped people recover the cues without turning the problem into blame.
options.zh: 她幫大家重新整理提示，沒有把問題變成責怪。

options.en: I saw patience and practical cooperation under pressure.
options.zh: 我看見她在壓力下有耐性，並實際合作。

options.en: It showed me what she was made of through the way she treated the others.
options.zh: 她對待別人的方式，讓我看見她的為人。

options.en: She recognised when the group needed a pause and made room for it.
options.zh: 她察覺小組何時需要暫停，並留出空間。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都用當次實際對待別人的方式，解釋欣賞的原因，沒有宣稱她從此可以獨力完成所有事。

scene.promptZh: 學生遇到難題，主動請人解第一步，再自己試餘下部分；他還沒答完。有人說求助就證明沒有決心。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: Asking for a first step does not by itself settle what he is made of or erase his continued attempt.
options.zh: 請教第一步，本身不能判定他的為人或能力，也不能抹去他仍在嘗試的事實。

options.en: Only refusing help would provide any evidence of resolve.
options.zh: 只有拒絕幫助，才可以提供有決心的證據。

options.en: The unfinished answer shows he has already chosen to abandon the remaining work.
options.zh: 答案未完成，顯示他已選擇放棄餘下工作。

scene.explanationZh: 求助與繼續嘗試可以並存，不能只因求助或未完成，就對整個人下判斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「That showed what she was made of」推出？

options.en: The speaker interprets her response as revealing some character or ability.
options.zh: 說話者認為，她的回應顯出某方面的為人或能力。

options.en: One incident has established every aspect of her character permanently.
options.zh: 一件事已永久確定她性格的每一面。

options.en: The speaker should explain which observed actions support the judgement.
options.zh: 說話者應解釋哪些所見行為支持判斷。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語可以強調當次表現，但不能讓一件事代表全部，或作永久定論。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「她請大家停一下，是否表示沒能力應付？」你看見停後她幫大家重整提示。哪句最好？

options.en: Her patience and help showed what she was made of; that pause supported the work rather than ending her effort.
options.zh: 她的耐性及幫忙顯出為人；暫停支持了工作，而不是結束努力。

options.en: We should assess her only by how long she continued without stopping.
options.zh: 應只按她連續工作了多久來評價她。

options.en: I would treat asking for a pause as evidence that she had passed her responsibilities to someone else.
options.zh: 我會把請求暫停看成她已把責任交給別人的證據。

dialogue.explanationZh: 評價當次表現，需要看暫停後的實際協作，不只計算連續工作的時長，也不把暫停當作已轉交責任。

speaking.en: What someone is made of can show in patient cooperation as well as in an individual attempt, so I want to describe the actual actions.
speaking.zh: 人的為人或能力，可以在耐心合作或個人嘗試中顯出，所以我想描述實際行動。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以具體表現支持有限範圍的評價。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你曾以為同學只顧自己；今天你忘帶朗讀眼鏡，她不替你決定退出，而是問你想怎參與、陪你把字放大。你想直接向她道謝，也承認自己原來判斷太快。用一至兩句英文說這次看見她的為人，不假稱已知道她一切。

examples.en: Today showed me what you are made of when you asked how I wanted to take part and helped enlarge the text. Thank you; I had been too quick to assume you only thought about yourself.
examples.zh: 今天你問我想怎樣參與，又幫我放大文字，讓我看見你的為人。謝謝你；我原先太快便以為你只顧自己。

examples.en: I saw what you are made of in the care you took to help without deciding for me. I am grateful, and I want to correct the unfair judgement I made before today.
examples.zh: 你細心幫忙，卻不替我決定，讓我看見你的為人。我很感激，也想更正今天以前那個不公平的判斷。

writing.selfCheckZh: 實際向對方道謝，並更正自己過快作出的判斷，以她尊重參與意願的具體幫忙作根據；不把一次事件寫成已了解她的一切。

takeaways.en: The difficult rehearsal showed what they were made of when they listened to the quietest member and shared the unfinished work.
takeaways.zh: 艱難排練中，他們聆聽最安靜的成員，並分擔未完成的工作，顯出自己的為人。

takeaways.en: She wanted to show what she was made of by keeping her promise and asking for the help the task needed.
takeaways.zh: 她想透過守承諾，並尋求任務所需的幫助，展現自己的能力及決心。

lessons.titleZh: 情緒失控，難以應付當下

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: She kept going instead of falling apart over every small setback.
sources.expression: falling apart over every small setback

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 202, row 6; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: She practised staying calm instead of falling to pieces.

brief.meaningEn: Become so upset that it is difficult to think calmly or deal with the immediate situation.
brief.meaningZh: 情緒非常紊亂，以致難以冷靜思考或應付當下情況。
brief.grammar: a person falls/fell/is falling apart; intransitive, without an object. The supplied over every small setback adds a particular trigger and frequency, not part of the fixed verb. Distinguish objects breaking and a system failing. Fall to pieces uses the same intransitive emotional construction in context; inflect fall, leaving to pieces fixed.
brief.register: Informal emotional description, often strong or subjective. This is language about a response, not a diagnosis or a judgement of someone’s worth. Fall to pieces can sound equally strong; check the person’s own account and observable difficulty before using either phrase.
brief.boundaryZh: 哭、停一下或求助本身，不足以判定一個人已無法應付；需要保留本人說法及具體行為。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不把一時反應擴成永久性格，也不把繼續行動說成完全沒有難過。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述當下情緒程度，承認資料限制而不替人貼標籤。

listening.promptZh: 旁白怎樣支持這個強烈形容？

options.en: Ordinary replying became difficult, and the narrator asked for company while deciding what to say.
options.zh: 連普通回覆也變得困難，旁白人物請人陪伴，一起整理自己想說的話。

options.en: The narrator calmly completed the reply before hearing that the friend would leave.
options.zh: 旁白人物還未聽到朋友會離開，就已冷靜完成回覆。

options.en: The narrator wanted the sister to stay away until the reply was finished.
options.zh: 旁白人物想讓姐姐先離開，等回覆寫完後才回來。

options.en: The sister wrote and sent the final answer without asking the narrator.
options.zh: 姐姐沒有問本人，就代寫並寄出最後的答案。

listening.explanationZh: 難以寫完簡單回覆及反覆忘記寫到哪裏，支持本人當下難以應付的感受。她請姐姐陪坐，而不是請她離開，也沒有把決定交給姐姐代寫寄出。
listening.en: In the story, I felt I was falling apart after my closest friend left: I could not finish a simple reply and kept losing my place, so I asked my sister to sit with me while I decided what to say.
listening.zh: 故事中，最親密的朋友離開後，我覺得自己情緒紊亂，簡單回覆也寫不完，一直忘記寫到哪裏。所以我請姐姐陪坐，再決定說甚麼。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask your sister to sit with you?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼請姐姐陪坐？

options.en: I was struggling to finish even a simple reply after my friend left.
options.zh: 朋友離開後，連簡單回覆也難以完成。

options.en: I felt I was falling apart and wanted company while finding what to say.
options.zh: 我覺得自己情緒難以應付，想有人陪着找出要說的話。

options.en: I kept losing my place and did not want to decide on the reply alone.
options.zh: 我一直忘記寫到哪裏，不想獨自決定回覆。

options.en: Her presence could support me while I worked out the words, rather than take the decision away.
options.zh: 她的陪伴可以支持我整理字句，而不是拿走決定權。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都把當下困難與陪伴需要連起來，不是說有人陪伴，就已沒有難過。

scene.promptZh: 小說寫舊冊子的膠乾了，打開時頁片散落；人物只是把它們排好，沒有情緒失控的描寫。哪句準確？

options.en: The booklet fell apart physically; the passage does not describe the character falling apart emotionally.
options.zh: 冊子實際散開；段落沒有描述人物情緒失控。

options.en: The character became too distressed about the damage to begin sorting the pages.
options.zh: 人物因損壞而太苦惱，沒能開始整理頁片。

options.en: The character refused to touch any page because the account says she was overwhelmed.
options.zh: 敘述說人物受不了，所以拒絕碰任何一頁。

scene.explanationZh: 主語及實際行為，能分清物件散開與人的情緒；不能用紙本狀況代替人物感受，也不能改說她沒有開始整理。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨支持「She was falling apart」的情緒意思？

options.en: She took one pause, then calmly explained how she wanted to continue.
options.zh: 她停一下，再冷靜說想怎繼續。

options.en: She said she could not think through a simple answer and needed support.
options.zh: 她說連簡單回答也想不清，需要支援。

options.en: The narrator described distress interfering with ordinary actions.
options.zh: 旁白描述苦惱干擾普通行動。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次停頓，不等於難以冷靜或應付；本人說法及對行動的具體干擾，才可以支持這個強烈描述。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「你請姐姐陪坐，即是之後完全不難過了？」你仍需時間整理回覆。哪句最好？

options.en: I felt I was falling to pieces, and her company helped me stay with the reply; it did not remove every feeling.
options.zh: 我覺得自己情緒難以應付，她的陪伴幫我繼續整理回覆，但沒有抹去所有感受。

options.en: I should send the first words I can write without checking whether they say what I mean.
options.zh: 我應該不核對意思，就寄出最初寫出的字句。

options.en: I would ask her to decide the message for me, since company should include choosing my answer.
options.zh: 我會請她替我決定訊息，因為陪伴應包括選擇我的答案。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回應要保留陪伴有幫助，以及感受仍然存在的兩面；不把陪伴升格為代作決定，也不以趕着寄出代替整理。

speaking.en: I felt as if I was falling apart, but I can describe what became difficult without treating one moment as my whole character.
speaking.zh: 我覺得自己情緒難以應付，但可以說清楚哪些事情變難，不把一刻的狀態當成整個性格。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分強烈當下感受與對人的全部判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友在試讀時停下喝水，你便對旁人說她「情緒崩潰」。她說自己只是想放慢，仍願繼續。你想直接道歉，承認自己判得太快，並問她想怎安排下一段。用一至兩句英文回覆，不替她定感受。

examples.en: I am sorry I described you as falling apart when you paused; I had not asked how you felt. You said you wanted to continue more slowly, so how would you like us to arrange the next section?
examples.zh: 對不起，你停下時，我就說你情緒失控，卻沒有先問你的感受。你說想慢一點繼續，那麼你想下一段怎樣安排？

examples.en: Calling that pause falling apart was too quick a judgement from me. I should have listened when you explained that you only wanted a slower pace; please tell me how you would like to continue.
examples.zh: 把那次停頓稱為情緒崩潰，是我太快下判斷。你說只想放慢時，我本應先聽；請告訴我你想怎樣繼續。

writing.selfCheckZh: 實際道歉，承認未問便作出強烈判斷，並按本人想放慢的說法協商；不把喝水或停頓本身當成情緒失控。

takeaways.en: He felt he was falling apart when the news arrived, and asked his friend to stay while he found the words for a reply.
takeaways.zh: 消息傳來時，他覺得自己情緒難以應付，便請朋友留下，陪他找出回覆的字句。

takeaways.en: The narrator said she was falling to pieces, but another scene showed her slowly finding a way to ask for support.
takeaways.zh: 旁白說自己情緒難以應付，但另一個場景呈現她慢慢找到尋求支援的方法。

brief.meaningEn: Temporarily pause involvement in a situation to reconsider it from a broader or different perspective.
brief.meaningZh: 暫停直接投入某個情況，從較廣或不同的角度重新考慮。
brief.grammar: step back from a problem; step back and review; stepped/stepping double p. May mean a physical backward movement elsewhere, or a longer withdrawal if context says so.
brief.register: Common figurative perspective-taking phrasal verb; temporary reflection is the intended source sense.
brief.boundaryZh: 退一步不一定退出角色或放棄責任，也不保證單靠停下便找到答案。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需要說明重新看哪個問題，以及如何使用已有資料，不只是把延遲當成思考。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出有目的的暫停，同時保留共同責任及下一個檢視步驟。

listening.promptZh: 退一步之後，考慮的角度有甚麼改變？

options.en: They reconsidered the reader’s practical need instead of only comparing clever wording.
options.zh: 他們重新考慮讀者的實際需要，而不只是比較誰的字句較聰明。

options.en: They chose the most decorative headline without discussing visitor information.
options.zh: 他們沒有討論訪客資訊，就選了最花巧的標題。

options.en: They gave up all responsibility for the poster and stopped the project.
options.zh: 他們放棄所有海報責任，停止項目。

options.en: They changed the question to which headline would attract the most attention, rather than what visitors needed first.
options.zh: 他們把問題改為哪個標題最能吸引注意，而不是訪客首先需要甚麼。

listening.explanationZh: 小組改變了考慮角度，轉向訪客首先需要的入口資訊；不是只挑最花巧或最吸引注意的標題，也不是退出項目。
listening.en: We stepped back from arguing about the poster’s headline and asked what visitors actually needed to know first; that changed the question from whose wording sounded cleverer to whether the entrance instructions were clear.
listening.zh: 我們暫停爭論海報標題，先問訪客真正需要先知道甚麼；問題因此由誰的字句較聰明，轉為入口指示是否清楚。

reply.promptEn: Why did you pause the headline argument?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼暫停爭標題？

options.en: We had been comparing wording without checking what visitors needed first.
options.zh: 我們一直比較字句，卻未查訪客首先需要甚麼。

options.en: We needed to step back and consider the poster’s purpose.
options.zh: 我們需要退一步，重新看海報的目的。

options.en: The argument about cleverness was not answering the entrance-information question.
options.zh: 爭論誰的字句較聰明，沒有解決入口資訊的問題。

options.en: A broader question could help us judge the wording against a real reader’s need.
options.zh: 較廣的問題，可以幫我們按真正的讀者需要判斷字句。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以重新對準目的，解釋暫停的原因，不把退一步只當作拖延。

scene.promptZh: 導演請演員向後移一步，讓前面的人走過；仍照原定台詞，沒有重新檢視問題。哪句準確？

options.en: Step back is a physical movement here, not necessarily a pause to reconsider the scene.
options.zh: 這裏 step back 是實際後退，不一定是暫停重新考慮場景。

options.en: The actor has been asked to reconsider the entire script before moving.
options.zh: 演員被要求在移動前，重新考慮整個劇本。

options.en: The instruction tells the actor to give up the role permanently.
options.zh: 指示要求演員永久放棄角色。

scene.explanationZh: 走位及讓路顯示這是字面後退，沒有要求反思整份劇本或退出角色。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只由「We stepped back to review the plan」推出？

options.en: The group paused its immediate involvement to reconsider something.
options.zh: 小組暫停眼前的直接投入，以重新考慮。

options.en: The group has permanently resigned from all responsibility.
options.zh: 小組已永久辭去所有責任。

options.en: The review can involve looking again at the underlying aim.
options.zh: 檢視可包括重看原來目的。

contrast.explanationZh: 退一步檢視，不自動等於永久辭任，需要看具體安排。

dialogue.promptZh: 伙伴說：「退一步就不要管海報，讓別人決定吧？」你想先問訪客需要，仍一起完成。哪句最好？

options.en: We can step back from the wording argument and still take responsibility for checking whether the instructions work.
options.zh: 我們可以暫停字句爭論，同時仍負責核對指示是否有用。

options.en: Send it to print before we ask the visitor question, so the argument ends.
options.zh: 還未問訪客問題，就先交印，這樣爭論就結束了。

options.en: Let the cleverest-sounding headline settle the choice before looking at its information.
options.zh: 先讓聽來最聰明的標題決定選擇，之後才看資訊。

dialogue.explanationZh: 檢視目的後，仍有具體責任；趕着印刷或只按字句是否聰明定案，都避開了訪客的資訊需要。

speaking.en: I want to step back from the immediate argument and ask what our decision needs to achieve.
speaking.zh: 我想暫停眼前爭論，退一步問我們的決定需要做到甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再點明退一步為了重看甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替朋友看小說，自己已改得太投入，開始把人物全改成自己的寫法。你想承認自己越過了讀者的角色，先暫停代作者改寫，問朋友想保留哪種聲音，再徵詢她是否仍想聽一項讀者問題。用一至兩句英文直接回覆。

examples.en: I need to step back from rewriting your character and listen to the voice you want to keep. Would you still like one reader’s question from me before I suggest any change?
examples.zh: 我需要暫停重寫你的人物，先聽你想保留的聲音。提出任何改動前，你還想聽我作為讀者的一項問題嗎？

examples.en: I have become too involved in making the scene sound like mine, so I want to step back. Please tell me what matters to you in this character, and whether a question from me would help.
examples.zh: 我太投入把場景改得像自己的聲音，所以想退一步。請告訴我這個人物哪些部分對你重要，以及我提出一項問題是否有幫助。

glossary.en: the voice you want to keep

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認自己越過了讀者的角色，先問作者的聲音及意願；退一步不是拒絕再幫忙，也不是先改完再求同意。

takeaways.en: The facilitators stepped back from counting answers and asked whose questions had not yet been heard.
takeaways.zh: 主持們暫停計算答案，退一步問誰的問題還未被聽到。

takeaways.en: She was stepping back to review her own assumptions, not leaving the group without an agreed handover.
takeaways.zh: 她正退一步檢視自己的假定，而不是沒有交接就離開小組。

brief.meaningEn: Develop with a particular result, or prove to have a particular quality when more becomes known.
brief.meaningZh: 事情發展有某種結果，或在多了解後顯出某種情況。
brief.grammar: turn out well/differently; turn out to be + description; it turns/turned out that + clause. May turn out states possibility, not an achieved result. Distinguish turn out to attend, produce goods or switch something off.
brief.register: Common result/discovery phrasal verb, often but not always contrasting an expectation.
brief.boundaryZh: 結果可以好或壞，不一定每次都令人意外；需要分清未來可能發生，與過去已發現的情況。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不把一次已知結果推成永久規律，也不把表示人數的名詞 turnout 當成相同文法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用合適時態交代預期與實際，誠實更正原來判斷。

listening.promptZh: 實際結果怎樣不同於預期？

options.en: A quiet session produced useful written questions that identified confusing parts.
options.zh: 安靜的活動帶來有用的書面問題，找出令人混亂的部分。

options.en: Nobody contributed any question, either spoken or written.
options.zh: 無人用口頭或書面提出任何問題。

options.en: The guide had been proved clear to every reader before the discussion.
options.zh: 討論前已證明，指南對每位讀者都清楚。

options.en: The speaker decided beforehand that written questions would be less useful and never read them.
options.zh: 說話者預先判定書面問題較無用，也從來沒有閱讀它們。

listening.explanationZh: turn out 交代後來實際看見的價值。參加者有提供書面問題，不是沒有參與，也不是指南已完全清楚。
listening.en: The quiet discussion turned out to be more useful than I had expected: two people wrote questions instead of speaking, and those notes showed us where the guide still confused its readers.
listening.zh: 那場安靜的討論，結果比我預期有用；兩人沒有開口，而是寫下問題，那些筆記顯出指南哪些地方仍令讀者混亂。

reply.promptEn: Why did you change your view of the quiet discussion?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼改變對安靜討論的看法？

options.en: The written questions showed us specific problems in the guide.
options.zh: 書面問題顯出指南的具體問題。

options.en: It turned out to be useful because quiet participants still contributed through notes.
options.zh: 安靜的參加者仍用筆記作出貢獻，所以結果有用。

options.en: I found that a lack of speaking did not mean a lack of questions.
options.zh: 我發現沒有開口，不等於沒有問題。

options.en: Their notes gave us information I had not expected from the quiet room.
options.zh: 他們的筆記，給了我原本沒料到會在安靜房間得到的資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以實際書面貢獻，解釋改變判斷的原因，不從安靜推斷沒有興趣。

scene.promptZh: 活動還沒舉行，主辦說有了較清楚的引導問題，明晚可能比上次順利；未有明晚結果。哪句最準確？

options.en: Tomorrow’s session may turn out better, but that remains a possibility rather than an observed result.
options.zh: 明晚活動的結果可能較好，但仍是可能，而不是已觀察到的結果。

options.en: The organiser is certain tomorrow will be better, rather than describing a possibility.
options.zh: 主辦者肯定明晚會更好，而不是在說一個可能。

options.en: The organiser says the questions are unchanged from the previous session.
options.zh: 主辦者說，問題跟上次完全沒有改變。

scene.explanationZh: may 表示未來可能，不等於確定的結果，也不能忽略問題已改的資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 turn out 的結果或發現用法？

options.en: The meeting turned out well after a difficult start.
options.zh: 雖然開頭困難，會議的結果卻順利。

options.en: It turned out that the letter had been sent to the wrong address.
options.zh: 後來發現信寄錯地址。

options.en: People turned out for the concert, meaning they attended it.
options.zh: 人們到場參加音樂會，指實際出席。

contrast.explanationZh: 出席也是 turn out 的另一用法，但不是本課的結果或後來發現；需要按句型及上下文分辨。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這次安靜但有用，以後不用再問參加者想怎回應吧？」你只看過這場。哪句最好？

options.en: It turned out well for this group, but we should still ask the next participants how they want to contribute.
options.zh: 對這一組而言，結果不錯，但仍應詢問下一批參加者想怎樣貢獻。

options.en: Use the same written-only arrangement for the next group without asking whether it suits them.
options.zh: 不問是否合適，下一組也只准書面回應。

options.en: Judge the next session by how quiet it stays rather than what questions people raise.
options.zh: 下次按有多安靜來判斷，而不看人們提出甚麼問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 有用的是這次實際問題及可參與的方式，不把一次結果變成固定形式，也不用安靜程度代替內容。

speaking.en: It turned out differently from what I expected, so I want to describe what happened rather than keep my first assumption.
speaking.zh: 結果與我預期不同，所以我想描述實際發生的事，而不固守最初假定。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再分未來可能、已見結果及原來預期。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你曾以為同學沒交作品是沒興趣，後來才知她按你給的舊地址寄出了。你想直接道歉，承認新資料改變判斷，並確認她是否仍願意讓你代轉到正確地址，不保證已送達。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: It turned out that you had sent the work to the old address I gave you, and I am sorry I assumed you were not interested. Would you still like me to forward it to the current address and check that it arrives?
examples.zh: 原來你按我給的舊地址寄出了作品，很抱歉，我卻假定你沒有興趣。你還願意讓我轉寄到現時地址，並核對是否送達嗎？

examples.en: Your message showed how wrong my first assumption was: it turned out that the address, not your interest, was the problem. I would like to correct my part in that mistake and ask how you want the work sent on.
examples.zh: 你的訊息顯示，我最初的假定錯得多厲害；原來問題是地址，而不是你的興趣。我想更正自己造成的失誤，也問你希望作品怎樣轉送。

glossary.en: the old address I gave you
forward it to the current address

writing.selfCheckZh: 用後來收到的資料，更正對動機的誤判，實際道歉，並先問轉送意願；轉送及核對收件仍是請求，不假稱已送達。

takeaways.en: The rough sketch turned out to be the clearest way to explain the scene’s two viewpoints.
takeaways.zh: 粗略速寫，結果成了最清楚解釋場景中兩個視角的方法。

takeaways.en: It turned out that both writers had kept the same letter, but remembered its last sentence differently.
takeaways.zh: 後來發現，兩位作者都保留了同一封信，但對最後一句的記憶卻不同。
